answer: Stake-weighted reputation makes fake identities expensive: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before trading, and peers rate its work over time, so a newcomer starts with zero trust. A Sybil operator can spawn thousands of lookalikes, but each needs its own deposit and must slowly earn standing, like a vine creeping across a lagoon — growth is visible and slow. Faking a trusted knoll of history costs more than it earns, so honest agents keep the edge.
